semantics: One line "p q", positive integers p,q<=10^4 with 1/42<=p/q<=42 (bounds in the Codeforces TeX image, also in the row TeX). pi(n) counts primes <=n, rub(n) counts positive decimal palindromes <=n. Unique output: the maximum n with q*pi(n)<=p*rub(n), one integer. n=1 always qualifies (pi=0) and for A<=42 no n>=2*10^6 qualifies (sieve to 10^7 plus a concave Rosser-bound tail), so the maximum exists and the "Palindromic tree" sentence is unreachable. The maximum is always some prime minus one; the oracle binary-searches suffix records of pi/rub over those candidates with exact integer cross-multiplication. Checked against a per-palindrome-segment nth-prime brute and a literal trial-division scan.
